Notation (from the preceding pages): [q] = prod_{n>=1}(1-q^n). Eq. 6 is the triple product sum_{n in Z} x^{n^2} y^n = prod_{n>=1}(1+x^{2n-1}y)(1+x^{2n-1}/y)·[x^2]. Write theta4(q) = 1-2q+2q^4-2q^9+... = [q]^2/[q^2] and theta3(q) = theta4(-q). Write P = prod_{n>=1}(1-x^{6n-3}) = [x^3]/[x^6].

(a) Opening line. Gauss divides the product form of eq. 26, x(1-x^3)(1-x^15)(1-x^21)(1-x^33)...[x^18] = x[x^3][x^18]^2/([x^6][x^9]), by xP. The result is [x^18]^2/[x^9] = psi(x^9) = sum_{k>=0} x^{9k(k+1)/2} = 1+x^9+x^27+x^54+x^90+...

[27] Hence x-x^4-x^16+x^25+x^49-x^64-... = P·x·psi(x^9). Here the left side is sum over n>0 with 3∤n of (-1)^{n-1}x^{n^2}. Gauss writes x·psi(x^9) as x^{-1/8}(x^{9/8}+x^{81/8}+x^{225/8}+x^{441/8}+...), i.e. exponents 9m^2/8 for odd m. This uses (9(2k+1)^2-1)/8 = 1+9k(k+1)/2.

[28] Eq. 24 states sum_{n in Z} q^{n(3n-1)/2} = [q^2][q^3]^2/([q][q^6]). Put q=x^3. Then theta4(x^9)/P = [x^6][x^9]^2/([x^3][x^18]) = 1+x^3+x^6+x^15+x^21+... So theta4(x^9) = P·x^{-1/8}·sum x^{m^2/8}, summed over m>0 coprime to 6 (exponents (m^2-1)/8 = 0,3,6,15,21,...).

[29] = [28] - 2·[27]. This uses theta4(x) - theta4(x^9) = -2(x-x^4-x^16+x^25+...). It gives theta4(x) = P x^{-1/8}{x^{1/8}-2x^{9/8}+x^{25/8}+x^{49/8}-2x^{81/8}+...}. The coefficient is +1 for gcd(m,6)=1 and -2 for 3|m.

[30] From Euler's pentagonal theorem (eq. 23) with x→x^3: x^{1/8}[x^3] = sum_{m>0} chi12(m) x^{m^2/8} = x^{1/8}-x^{25/8}-x^{49/8}+x^{121/8}+x^{169/8}-... Since theta4(x^3) = [x^3]^2/[x^6] = P[x^3], this gives theta4(x^3) = P x^{-1/8}{...}.

[31] = [29]+[30]. theta4(x)+theta4(x^3) = 2P x^{-1/8}{x^{1/8}-x^{9/8}-x^{81/8}+x^{121/8}+x^{169/8}-x^{225/8}-...}. Here m ≡ ±1 (mod 12) gives +, m ≡ ±3 (mod 12) gives -, and m ≡ ±5 (mod 12) cancels.

[32] = [28]+[30]. theta4(x^3)+theta4(x^9) = 2P x^{-1/8}{x^{1/8}+x^{121/8}+x^{169/8}+x^{529/8}+...}, summed over m ≡ ±1 (mod 12).

(b) In eq. 6 Gauss substitutes x→x^6, y→xy. This gives prod(1+x^{12n-5}y)(1+x^{12n-7}/y)·[x^12] = sum_n x^{6n^2+n} y^n = 1+x^5/y+x^7y+x^22/y^2+x^26y^2+...

With m=12n+1 we have (m^2-1)/8 = 18n^2+3n. So, putting x→x^3 and y=1, the sum in [32] is prod(1+x^{36n-15})(1+x^{36n-21})·[x^36].

[33] theta4(x^3)+theta4(x^9) = 2[x^36]·P·(1+x^15)(1+x^21)(1+x^51)(1+x^57)...
[34] (x^3→x in [33]) theta4(x)+theta4(x^3) = 2[x^12]·prod(1-x^{2n-1})·prod(1+x^{12n-7})(1+x^{12n-5}).
[35],[36] are [33],[34] with x→-x, giving the theta3 versions with signs flipped in the factors.

Final remark (Gauss): since the left side of [31] equals that of [34], the bracket in [31] factors as well. Explicitly (my step): x^{-1/8}{...}_{31} = [x][x^6][x^12]/([x^2][x^3])·prod(1+x^{12n-5})(1+x^{12n-7}).

Purpose: a systematic derivation of product formulas for sums and differences of theta-nulls theta(q), theta(q^3), theta(q^9), i.e. level-3/9/12 theta relations. The page continues the cubic/level-3 analogue of the quadratic theta relations used for the AGM on the previous page; the next page treats differences and products.

Notational looseness only: the left sides of [31]-[36] are written as truncated finite brackets {1-2x+2x^4-2x^9} without '&c.'

results.modern_name: Jacobi triple product / Euler pentagonal number theorem

results.what: theta4(x) - theta4(x^9) = -2x·prod(1-x^{6n-3})·psi(x^9) (eq. 27/29); dissection of theta by n mod 3
results.usually_credited_to: Ramanujan's notebooks (Berndt, Part III); implicit in cubic transformation work of Legendre/Jacobi

results.what: Product formulas theta(q)+theta(q^3) = 2[q^12]·prod(1-q^{2n-1})·prod(1+q^{12n-5})(1+q^{12n-7}) and the theta3 analogue (eqs. 33-36)
results.modern_name: Level-12 theta-function identity (cf. Ramanujan's phi(q)+phi(q^3) relations; Schröter-type formulas)
results.usually_credited_to: Ramanujan (notebooks), proved by Berndt et al.; derivable from Schröter (1854)

deep.surprise_reason: Gauss's possession of the triple product, the theta product formulas and modular-type theta relations in the Nachlass is well documented (Werke III, VIII). Explicit level-3/9/12 identities such as theta(q)+theta(q^3) as an infinite product, of the type usually cited from Ramanujan's notebooks, are a notable unpublished detail. They follow routinely from the triple product, however, and similar items are known from his papers.
